newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada oil industry financings soar 132 pct in '96.
newsitem.headline: Canada oil industry financings soar 132 pct in '96.

text.p: Treasury financings in the Canadian oil industry surged to a record C$9.5 billion in 1996, up 132 percent from the previous year, Calgary-based brokerage Sayer Securities Ltd said on Wednesday.
In a report, Sayer said the money raised last year flowed from 494 issues, a jump from C$4.1 billion raised through 375 issues in 1995.
"Healthy commodity prices, low interest rates and strong investor interest made it relatively easy for oil companies to raise money in 1996," Sayer said.
Among the financings in 1996, equity offerings accounted for C$4.6 billion, 57 percent more than the record set in 1993. Debt issues totaled C$2.8 billion, 52 percent above last year, Sayer said.
Company research manager Sarah Clayton said in an interview that several signs pointed to another strong year in 1997.
"As long as the market fundamentals stay healthy the way they are right now, there's a good chance we'll see financings happening," Clayton said.
Junior oil companies were big benefactors of last year's enthusiastic investment climate, Sayer said.
Eleven initial public offerings were completed for a value of C$107.2 million. The figure excluded IPOs valued at under C$1 million.
The 1996 IPO showing, however, was well below that of 1993 when a record 32 energy issues were floated for a total of C$684.5 million.

Not included in the IPO total were royalty trusts, which became extremely popular in 1996. Eleven new trusts -- companies that use cash flow from operations to pay regular distributions to holders, rather than invest in new exploration -- were formed for a total of C$1.6 billion.
Six previously established trusts raised an additional C$527.6 million, Sayer said.

The brokerage also said C$1 billion was raised in 1996 by more than 20 companies to fund projects outside Canada, including locations in Sudan, Turkey, Greenland, India, Equador, Libya, Qatar, Cuba and Ukraine.
